title: 5 Claude Code Skills That Save You Hours

slides.title: 5 Claude Code *skills* that save you *hours*
slides.sub: Built into Claude Code. One slash command each.

slides.title: Stop retyping the same *prompts.*
slides.lede: A *skill* is a saved playbook. Type `/name` and Claude follows it.

slides.title: Tidy your changes *before* anyone reviews them.
slides.text: Reviews your changed code for cleanup opportunities, then applies the fixes.
slides.watch: `/simplify` does not look for correctness bugs. Use `/code-review` for that.

slides.title: A second pair of eyes, on *demand.*
slides.text: Reviews your diff, a PR number, a branch, or a path for correctness bugs.
slides.watch: `/review` is an alias. `ultra` runs a deeper review in the cloud.

slides.title: One instruction. *Many* parallel agents.
slides.text: Splits a large change into independent units and works on them in parallel.
slides.watch: Needs a git repository (or a `WorktreeCreate` hook). Review the plan before approving.

slides.title: Let Claude *babysit* it for you.
slides.text: Runs a prompt again and again on an interval. Skip the interval and Claude paces itself.
slides.watch: It runs only while your session stays open.

slides.title: Ask Claude to read its *own logs.*
slides.text: Turns on debug logging for this session, then troubleshoots from the log.
code: {{p:>}} {{c:/debug}} the build hangs after I save
slides.watch: Logging is off by default. `/debug` captures from that moment forward, not before.
